final.narration: Since the 2024-12-17 visit, measurements at the Pigeon River near Hepco, USGS 03459500, sit 33 % below the rating, so published flows run that much too high. For a given flow rate, the river stands 0.33 ft higher than the curve predicts; at a stage of 2.33 ft it carries about 150 cfs (26 %) less than the curve's 570 cfs. The hydrographer noted "Scour control changed" on 2024-12-17. In the note's terms, the control (the riffle just downstream that sets the water level) eroded, so a given flow rate passes at a lower water level. That disagrees with the data. After the change, at that stage, area fell 11 % and velocity fell 22 %, so the flow rate there fell about 31 %, which agrees with the 26 % drop in measured flow rate. Hurricane Helene (2024-09-27) passed between the 2024-08-22 and 2024-12-17 visits; no gauging was made during the storm. DriftWatch's agents rank fill first (45 %); the hydrographer's note says scour; the two disagree, so the cause is not settled. Double-check: Survey the control section and downstream reach for deposited sediment or debris, and recheck the gauge datum against reference marks. Rating confidence 24/100 (Stale).

final.skeptic_argument: The observed residual is strongly negative at -33.1%, which rules out scour and fits fill/backwater or a datum issue. But the channel geometry shows only a modest area decrease (-11.3%) while velocity fell much more (-22.1%), which is more consistent with downstream backwater/fill than with a pure datum change.
